summary:
# NOTES ON: "ONLY ONE LOVE; Or, Who Was The Heir?" by Charles Garvice (Gutenberg #35523)

Single novel. Followed by publisher ad pages (M. A. Donohue & Co., Chicago) which are not story content.

## Setting / Places
- Forest of Warden (England); Gideon's cottage in a clearing; Wermesley (rail village, "Spotted Boar" inn); Arkdale (county town, 4.5-5 mi, "Bush" inn is at Hurst Leigh village); Hurst Leigh / "The Hurst" (Squire's mansion, Wealdshire); Walmington Square (Mrs. Davenant's London house); Park Lane (Lady Bell's house); Spider Court, Temple (Jack & Leonard's rooms, No. 5); The Albany (Stephen's chambers); Hawks' Club; Earl's Court (Lady Bell's country place, ~13 mi from Hurst); Cheltenham Terrace (Laura's lodging); Clumley (church for wedding); Netherton (inn, change of horses); Thames Dutton/Hampton Court/Richmond (picnic); Strand restaurant.

## Characters
- **Jack Newcombe** ("the Savage"), 22, gentleman, Oxford-educated, spendthrift, drinker, loves Una. Heir expected but disinherited; left only nothing ("not even a mourning-ring"). Owes money to Levy Moss (money-lender). Gives "post obit" bill. Rows, drives, boxes, fences.
- **Una Rolfe / Eunice Davenant**, 21 (eighteen years in Warden; age 3 when arrived), beautiful, dark-brown eyes, bright brown/bronze hair, raised by woodman Gideon; reads books; never schooled. Real daughter of Ralph Davenant and Caroline Hatfield.
- **Gideon Rolfe**, woodman, former schoolmaster's son at Hurst; loved Caroline Hatfield (gamekeeper's daughter); Ralph Davenant (school friend) eloped with her. Keeps deerhound **Dick**. Speaks with dialect "thee".
- **Martha Rolfe**, Gideon's wife, Una's "mother"; cries at parting.
- **Ralph Davenant** ("Squire Davenant"), 80, dying; dissolute then miser; sardonic; calls Stephen "hound", "oily eel".
- **Stephen Davenant**, nephew & supposed heir; pale, sleek, black hair, light gray eyes, "private view of a cemetery" smile; "Fascination Davenant". Steals will; forges/hides; attempts to marry Una; plots.
- **Mrs. Davenant** (Stephen's mother), nervous, timid, lives Walmington Square, maid **Jane**.
- **Laura Treherne** (aka Mary Burns as maid), ~22, Stephen's pledged fiancée, grandfather old Mr. Treherne (died); tall, dark, passionate; warns Stephen "Remember!"; later Lady Bell's maid; Leonard's love.
- **Mr. Hudsley**, old solicitor (James Hudsley); withdraws after estate settled.
- **Skettle**, Hudsley's thin wrinkled clerk; son Ned (Jack saved from mill-pond); keeps scrap of will; ultimately proves the will.
- **Slummers**, Stephen's valet ("the Shadow"), silent, hates Jack (Jack kicked him).
- **Sir Humphrey**, physician (30 guineas).
- **Jobson**, landlord of Bush; **South**, miller; tailor; parish clerk.
- **Leonard Dagle**, Jack's barrister friend and fellow lodger, Spider Court; loves Laura (locket).
- **Lady Isabel "Bell" Earlsley**, millionairess, "Wild Bird" (Una's nickname), brougham, Jackson coachman; father a bookworm, Earl's Court; companion **Mrs. Fellowes**.
- **Dalrymple** (Marquis/Lord, "Dally"), **Sir Arkroyd Hetley** ("Ark"), friends; **Lady Pierrepoint** (Countess), **Lady Clarence**, **Mrs. Cantrip**, Duke of Garnum ("little duke").
- **Levy Moss**, money-lender; **Dr./Lady Merivale** (ball hostess).
- **Cook/Mary** (maid at Walmington).

## BOOK PLOT, in order
1. Jack lost in Warden Forest at dusk; sings "Oh, wake and call me early"; follows woodman Gideon's dog Dick; Gideon refuses entry, gives cider and cake, points road to Arkdale; Jack's dollar refused. Gideon recognizes face. Una returns; Jack forces door; Gideon hands him to chair; Una's touch stops violence. Jack says he is Jack Newcombe going to Squire Davenant at Hurst Leigh.
2. Jack sleeps on fox-skins; Gideon: "Faces of angels and the hearts of devils." Jack leaves at dawn; note with ring for Mrs. Rolfe (ring taken from little finger; sovereign offered).
3. Lakeside: Una and Jack talk; wasp; kiss on hand; Jack learns Una never left Warden; he confesses being "bad lot", money lost, post obit. Dog-rose gift. Gideon attacks Jack with stick; "I warned you, viper"; Jack vows to return.
4. Hurst: Ralph dying; Stephen posts messages; Jack arrives late; Ralph forgives loosely. Stephen opens Ralph's safe; Ralph says "Hudsley"; Stephen impersonates Hudsley's voice; takes two wills (first will to Stephen, July will). Hudsley arrives; Stephen steals the July will, Ralph dies crying "You thief!".
5. Stephen flees with stolen will; reads it: £50,000 to Jack; Black's sermons (29 vols) to Stephen; servants £100 each; remainder to daughter Eunice Davenant, trustee Hudsley; reveals secret marriage to Caroline Hatfield at Armfield church, June; daughter kept by Gideon Rolfe. Stephen nearly burns it but keeps it. Laura taps window; she came from London, followed Slummers, says "Remember!"
6. Laura leaves; Stephen searches for dropped will; attacks Jack on lawn; Jack says no. Stephen writes to mother to meet him at Wermesley. Jack goes to Bush inn.
7. Villagers gossip; funeral; will read: Stephen gets everything; Jack nothing. Jack leaves Hurst.
8. Gideon's cottage empty; Jack to Spider Court; Leonard meets Laura on train, tracks her to Cheltenham Terrace. Jack at Hawks' Club, drinks champagne; Lady Bell's brougham nearly runs over him; she takes him home; Leonard receives card.
9. Stephen takes Una to London; Mrs. Davenant. Una meets Lady Bell at jeweler; ball at Park Lane; Jack and Una meet; Una's rose; Una's song on the river at Richmond.
10. Jack and Una love declared, Jack tells Una of his poverty; Mrs. Davenant hosts Jack; "Yes, dear, I love but thee" song. Stephen sees them. Stephen plots: frames Jack for debts (buys bills via Moss); plans marriage; Gideon brought in.
11. Gideon confronts Stephen; Stephen's ploy: Una's illegitimacy story; Jack's letter of break-off (Stephen reads it over steam). Una and Jack separated. Jack and Lady Bell nearly marry; Lady Bell refuses Jack ("Is—No"), kisses him.
12. Stephen's wedding plot: license, carriage to Clumley; horses missing at Netherton; Laura and Gideon appear; Jack returns; Skettle produces the July will fragment; Stephen loses.
13. Epilogue: Jack and Una married in spring at Hurst; Gideon attends; Stephen a charity philanthropist living on a quarterly check from Jack's lawyer.

## Key quoted phrases
- "Only one love" ; "Remember!" (Laura) ; "Yes, dear, I love but thee" ; "It is false!" (Una) ; "Tell him." (Jack) ; "Tell him—Mr. Stephen" ; "Thief!" (Ralph).
